biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very adverse; strongly associated with poor outcome in t-AML

biomarkers.name: Complex and monosomal karyotype, -5/-7 abnormalities
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adverse; classically associated with alkylating agent/radiation-related cases

biomarkers.name: KMT2A (MLL) rearrangements
biomarkers.prevalence: Subset of cases, classically associated with prior topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure and short latency
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defines a recurrent fusion subtype; relevant to menin inhibitor trials

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: AML morphology (as per AML_NOS) with clinical history of prior cytotoxic exposure
variants: alkylating agent-related (long latency 5-10y, -5/-7, TP53, complex karyotype, preceded by MDS phase)
topoisomerase II inhibitor-related (short latency 1-3y, KMT2A rearrangements, no preceding MDS phase, often monocytic differentiation)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: As per AML_NOS; often reflects prior treatment-induced clonal haematopoiesis

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: HSC or committed myeloid progenitor with prior cytotoxic exposure history
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: AML morphology similar to de novo AML but with enrichment for adverse cytogenetics (TP53, complex, -5/-7 for alkylator-related) or characteristic fusions (KMT2A for topoisomerase II-related)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Two distinct pathways reflect different mechanisms: alkylating agent-related (long latency 5-10 years, TP53-driven, often preceded by MDS phase); topoisomerase II inhibitor-related (short latency 1-3 years, KMT2A rearrangements, no preceding MDS phase, often monocytic differentiation)
